Evolution of local populations

Source: R/evolution.R
evolution_control.Rd

Settings for the evolution of the niche optimum within each population (a species at a site) during simulate_metacommunity() or mc_dynamics(). Without them, every population of a species keeps the optimum of the species. With them, each population has its own genetic mean \(\bar z\), which responds to selection by the local environment, drifts, mixes with immigrants and starts from a sample of its founders.

Usage

evolution_control(
  genetic_var,
  ne_ratio = 1,
  plasticity = 0,
  env_var = 0,
  steps_per_generation = 1,
  founder = TRUE,
  env = NULL,
  traits = NULL
)

Arguments

genetic_var

Additive genetic variance of the optimum \(G\), in squared units of the environment, one value or one per species.

ne_ratio

Ratio of effective to census population size \(\nu\); Inf turns drift off.

plasticity

Slope of the reaction norm b, one value or one per species: 0 for a fixed phenotype, 1 for a phenotype that tracks the environment fully around \(E_0\).

env_var

Environmental (non-heritable) variance of the phenotype \(V_E\), one value or one per species.

steps_per_generation

Time steps per generation \(g\); selection and drift per step are divided by it (at least 1); dispersal and demography are per step.

founder

Should populations founded at a step start from the sampled mean of their founders (TRUE) or from the mean of their source (FALSE)?

env, traits

The environment of each site (a vector, or a function of the step that returns one) and the traits of the species (from species_traits()). Filled in by simulate_metacommunity(); needed only with mc_dynamics().

Value

An mc_evolution object, to pass as evolution.

Details

At each step, in the order of the model:

  1. Seeds carry the optimum of the species in traits, the mean of a regional pool that does not evolve. They mix with residents in proportion to their numbers; a population founded by seeds alone starts as below.

  2. Phenotype and growth. The phenotype is \(p = \bar z + b (E - E_0)\), a linear reaction norm with slope plasticity (b) around the reference environment \(E_0\), the mean environment of the sites at the first step. The plastic part is immediate and reversible: every individual, migrants included, grows with the phenotype of the site where it is. Growth is the mean fitness of a population whose phenotypes are normal around \(p\) with variance \(P = G + V_E\), under the Gaussian response of growth_rates(): \(r = r_{max} \sqrt{\sigma^2 / (\sigma^2 + P)} \exp(-(E - p)^2 / (2(\sigma^2 + P)))\). The variance widens the response and lowers its peak (the load); with \(P = 0\) it is the response of growth_rates().

  3. Selection and drift, in each population present after reproduction (\(N > 0\)): $$\Delta \bar z = \frac{1}{g} \frac{G}{\sigma^2 + P} (E - p) + \epsilon, \quad \epsilon \sim N\left(0, \frac{G}{g N_e}\right), \quad N_e = \nu N,$$ the response to Gaussian stabilising selection of Lande (1976), with additive genetic variance \(G\) (genetic_var), phenotypic variance \(P = G + V_E\) (env_var), the niche breadth \(\sigma\) of the species as the width of the fitness function, \(g\) steps per generation (steps_per_generation) and the ratio \(\nu\) of effective to census size (ne_ratio), the same fitness function as in growth. \(G\) is constant: it does not erode with drift nor grow when divergent populations mix.

  4. Gene flow. After dispersal, the genetic mean of a population is the mean of residents and immigrants weighted by their numbers. Immigrants carry the mean of the populations they come from, weighted by the emigrants each sends through the dispersal kernel (or, on spatially implicit landscapes, by the emigrants of all other sites). A population with no residents after reproduction and emigration (absent, or lost all its members) is founded by its \(k\) immigrants: with founder = TRUE, their mean is drawn from \(N(\bar z_{in}, (G + V_B)/k)\), the sampling of a few individuals, where \(V_B\) is the variance among the means of their sources, weighted as above. Populations present at the start and those founded by seeds alone are drawn in the same way around the optimum of the species. Immigrants into a population with residents carry the expected mean of their sources, without sampling noise. The phenotype recorded after dispersal (phenotype in the output) mixes residents and immigrants still carrying the plastic response to their site of origin, as when individuals are sampled right after dispersal; it does not enter the dynamics.

  5. Populations lost to extirpation, competition or the pool lose their mean.

Species with \(G = 0\) keep the optimum of the species exactly and draw no random numbers, so with genetic_var = 0, env_var = 0 and plasticity = 0 the abundances are the same as without evolution for the same seed. With mc_dynamics(), growth rates come from env and traits of evolution, and r only sets the numbers of sites and species.

Two cases have known answers, checked in the tests of the package. A population alone, without selection (very wide niche) and of constant size \(N\), accumulates a variance of \(G t / (\nu N)\) after \(t\) generations (Lande 1976). Two populations of the same size in environments \(E_1\) and \(E_2\), exchanging a share \(m\) of individuals each generation, with selection \(a = G / (\sigma^2 + P)\) and no drift, reach the divergence \(d^* = (1 - 2m) a (E_1 - E_2) / (1 - (1 - 2m)(1 - a))\), which follows from the recursion of the steps above.

References

Lande, R. (1976). Natural selection and random genetic drift in phenotypic evolution. Evolution, 30, 314–334. doi:10.1111/j.1558-5646.1976.tb00911.x

See also

Other simulate metacommunities: colonisation_history(), growth_rates(), logistic_gradients(), mc_dynamics(), simulate_logistic(), simulate_metacommunity(), simulate_static()

Examples

set.seed(1)
ls <- landscape_implicit(20)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(10)
traits <- species_traits(tr)
sim <- simulate_metacommunity(ls, traits, competition_matrix(tr, "phylo"),
                              dispersal = 0.001, n_steps = 300,
                              evolution = evolution_control(genetic_var = 4, ne_ratio = 0.5))
# local genetic means follow the environment of each site
head(sim$evolution$genetic[, 1:4])
#>             t1       t2       t3       t4
#> site1 33.82137 35.20115       NA 19.62512
#> site2 41.21913       NA 37.06979 23.92967
#> site3 57.64955 65.25984 57.58140 48.50037
#> site4 88.43806 91.00418 92.88088       NA
#> site5 28.77965 67.32722       NA 13.15587
#> site6 85.50623 91.24391 89.18069       NA
